PHASE.NAME: UPGRADE_4 Context Pressure Integration Gate
PHASE.GOAL: Implement T6 context pressure monitoring and run the full UPGRADE_4 token economy verification gate.

DATA_FLOWS.FLOW: Tracker estimates current session context pressure from input tokens, output tokens, and configured context_window_limit.
MCP responses include _context_pressure for critical state and _auto_recommendation for agent_resume above 90 percent pressure.
tools/list automatically switches to terse at high or critical pressure.
CI and parity tests prove the combined T1-T8 token economy layer remains backward-compatible.

STEPS.step-1: Add context_window_limit to budget config with a conservative default and config-key update support.
STEPS.step-2: Add ContextPressure and PressureLevel with low, moderate, high, and critical thresholds.
STEPS.step-4: Append critical pressure metadata and agent_resume recommendation to tool responses.
STEPS.step-5: Force terse tools/list output when pressure is high or critical.
STEPS.step-6: Add an UPGRADE_4 token economy gate covering profiles, terse schemas, response trimming, cache hints, recommendations, compaction, budget, and pressure.
STEPS.step-7: Update docs parity so public token economy claims match implemented behavior.

VERIFICATION.CHECK: cargo run --quiet -- mcp stdio with tools/list profile=verification style=terse
context_pressure reports low, moderate, high, and critical thresholds correctly.
pressure above 90 percent includes agent_resume auto recommendation.
syn refresh --json reports no canonical drift.
syn status reports healthy token economy state.

RISKS.RISK: Pressure estimates are approximate because external chat context is not fully observable; report as estimate and make thresholds configurable.
Automatic terse output can surprise clients; only force it under high/critical pressure and include explicit metadata.
Combined T1-T8 changes touch MCP protocol surfaces; keep default requests backward-compatible throughout implementation.
